title: When the Terminal Breaks
premise: Beatrix Hartwell, a cargo hauler who once investigated impossible accidents for the Meridian Insurance Consortium, is the only witness to a nine-second gravity failure that coincides with the erasure of an entire mining colony's records. As she digs into the anomaly, she uncovers evidence that the colony of Vesper's Reach was massacred to cover up a failed terraforming experiment, and that the system-wide flicker was the weapon misfiring. Hunted by consortium enforcers and betrayed by her oldest friend, Beatrix must smuggle the colony's surviving memory cores to the last functioning Earth relay before its transmission loop decays forever. She succeeds at terrible cost, broadcasting the truth as her ship burns, and dies knowing the massacre can no longer be denied.
about_author: Felix Vane is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. He writes from a houseboat off the coast of Maine, where he claims the fog helps him remember what forgetting feels like.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. While hauling ore through contested orbits, Beatrix experiences nine seconds of weightlessness that shouldn't be possible, and every instrument aboard insists it never happened. Her old investigator instincts stir for the first time in fifteen years. Emotional beat: unease—the past knocking on a door she welded shut.

chapters.title: The Claim That Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A widow files an insurance claim for a husband who died on Vesper's Reach—a colony whose records show it was never inhabited. Beatrix recognizes the claim format from her Consortium days and realizes someone is using her old methods against the system itself. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Ghost Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Following shipping lanes through blacklisted space, she finds physical debris from Vesper's Reach: personal effects, children's toys, a mass grave's thermal shadow. The colony held eleven thousand people. Emotional beat: grief arriving early, before proof, like a premonition she resents.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: POV alternating Beatrix and Consortium adjuster Ivo Renk. Renk, Beatrix's former protégé, is dispatched to make her problem disappear. He admires her even as he falsifies her flight logs. Emotional beat: the chilling intimacy of institutional violence—polite, procedural, certain.

chapters.title: Memory Cores
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A dying colonist engineer, Sefa, gives Beatrix three memory cores containing raw sensor data of the massacre, hidden inside a gravity regulator—the same device type that caused the nine-second flicker. Emotional beat: the crushing weight of being chosen as a witness when survival was the only skill she trusted herself with.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years Invisible
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, flashback-heavy. We learn why Beatrix left the Consortium: she once certified a fraudulent report that ruined an innocent captain, and chose obscurity over penance. Now the same cowardice offers her an exit—sell the cores, disappear again. Emotional beat: self-loathing confronting its own reflection.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Docking Bay Seven
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Her oldest friend and broker, Tam, sells her location to Renk to pay his own debts. Beatrix escapes the ambush but loses her ship's long-range drive and one core. Emotional beat: betrayal not as shock but as confirmation of every reason she stopped trusting people.

chapters.title: The Loop Is Ending
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix and Renk. Earth's last transmission relay enters final decay; in seventy hours it goes dark permanently, and with it any channel the truth could ride. Renk corners Beatrix with an offer: amnesty for the cores. She realizes he genuinely believes the massacre was mercy. Emotional beat: horror at how conviction and cruelty wear the same face.

chapters.title: Burn Toward Earth
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. In a stolen tug with failing life support, Beatrix runs the relay blockade while Renk pursues. She triggers the remaining gravity regulators to disable his ships, accepting that the same weapon will tear her vessel apart. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve—she finally spends herself on something true.

chapters.title: What the Records Say Now
chapters.summary: POV shifting to listeners across the system. The transmission loop carries the massacre data outward one final time before Earth goes silent. Colonists' names are read aloud; Renk resigns in disgrace; Tam funds a memorial he'll never be forgiven into. Beatrix's last recorded words close the book. Emotional beat: mourning braided with vindication—the price paid, the truth kept.
